goal: Users explicitly open and persist one Markdown workspace through honest desktop or Web capabilities while unsaved text remains excluded from validation and build.
non_goals: Do not create React, TypeScript, Vite, HTTP, Tauri, native-dialog, or sidecar implementation.
Do not implement browser-native filesystem APIs or expose arbitrary browser paths.
Do not add autosave, recent files, multi-document state, file watching, or conflict resolution.
Do not implement template UI, diagnostics localization, outline, preview, or build cancellation.
Do not change parser, validator, compiler, renderer, application services, or DOCX behavior.
expected_evidence: Observed strict-TDD RED for missing source lifecycle APIs and atomic filesystem adapter
Atomic writer tests covering replacement, cleanup, UTF-8, Save As, and preservation on injected failure
Controller tests covering desktop open/save, Web workspace/download capabilities, dirty guards, recovery, and post-save refresh ordering
Tests proving inspect, validate, and build receive persisted paths and never mutate source files
Focused and full pytest, Ruff, pip check, strict OpenSpec, SpecNav entry, CodeGraph, JSON, and whitespace evidence
Task report, dedicated spec review, and dedicated quality review
unsafe_assumptions: A browser can access arbitrary native paths.
Writable Web workspaces and upload/download-only sources expose identical actions.
A save may update the saved snapshot before persistence succeeds.
A post-save refresh failure means the atomic write did not happen.
Editing or cancellation may safely race an in-flight source persistence operation.
Portable permission behavior can be tested only with chmod rather than injected failures.
stop_condition: Stop if implementation requires edits outside the eight allowed source/test files, duplicates compiler behavior, exposes browser-native paths, weakens atomic replacement, or cannot separate persistence success from refresh failure.
